holiday_plan.intro: Thanksgiving was yesterday; prioritize November 27–29 now. A four-day weekend requires Friday off, and employer time off is not assumed. These destinations fit roughly a three-hour normal-traffic driving radius, but holiday traffic can take longer. Cold Spring and Philadelphia are car-free choices; Hudson offers a one-night escape.

trips.title: Cold Spring: industrial ruins, woodland and village food
trips.why: Combine West Point Foundry Preserve's woodland trails and historic ironworks remains with Main Street shops and a meal. The preserve is free and open year-round, dawn to dusk.
trips.transport: Car-free: Metro-North Hudson Line from Grand Central to Cold Spring, then walk. Do not rely on the seasonal village trolley; its published season ends at Veterans Day.
trips.time_budget: Allow a full day, keeping the preserve walk within daylight.
trips.booking_note: No preserve admission ticket is needed. Verify your outbound and return trains and individual restaurant holiday hours; date-specific rail service was not confirmed.

trips.title: Hudson overnight with Olana's special holiday house access
trips.why: Pair Hudson's restaurants and shops with Frederic Church's designed landscape and art-filled house. November 27–28 brings special self-paced house access, while the newly opened Laurent Grasso installation adds contemporary art.
trips.transport: Car-required for this proposed itinerary. Olana also lists Amtrak to Hudson plus a taxi, but explicitly warns that local taxi and rideshare service is limited; that alternative needs confirmed round-trip transfers.
trips.time_budget: One night, November 27–28 or 28–29. Olana estimates a 2.5-hour drive from NYC before holiday delays.
trips.booking_note: November 27–28 house visits require Explore at Your Own Pace timed tickets; last ticketed entry is 3:15 p.m., with the house closing at 4 p.m. Sunday uses the regular tour offerings. Grounds open daily, 8 a.m. to sunset. Confirm lodging, meals and ticket inventory separately.
trips.event_name: The Artist's House: Explore at Your Own Pace

trips.title: Philadelphia: market lunch and German-style holiday stalls
trips.why: Visit Reading Terminal Market for food, then explore Christmas Village at LOVE Park and City Hall. Friday or Saturday is preferable if Pennsylvania Dutch merchants are a priority; they close Sundays.
trips.transport: Car-free: NJ TRANSIT Northeast Corridor from New York Penn to Trenton, then SEPTA Trenton Line to Center City. Amtrak to Philadelphia is another option, but its official pages were blocked during research.
trips.time_budget: A full day with substantial rail travel; allow connection time at Trenton rather than planning a tight turnaround.
trips.booking_note: Reading Terminal lists 8 a.m.–6 p.m. regular hours and was closed November 26; merchant hours vary. Christmas Village lists noon–9 p.m. November 27–28 and noon–8 p.m. November 29, with no admission charge. Verify both rail operators' holiday schedules and separate fares.

trips.title: Longwood's astronomy-themed Christmas gardens
trips.why: A distinctive indoor-outdoor holiday outing: conservatory planting displays, an astronomer's-observatory installation and illuminated gardens, with a garden railway operating weather permitting.
trips.transport: Car-required for the proposed driving itinerary. Longwood also advertises direct OurBus service from NYC, but departures and return service for this weekend were not verified; do not assume that alternative operates on your date.
trips.time_budget: A long day extending into the evening, near the outer edge of the requested driving radius. Longwood lists 130 miles from New York; holiday delays can push travel beyond three hours each way.
trips.booking_note: The official season page lists daily hours of 10 a.m.–11 p.m. Timed admission is required; ticket availability was not checked. Most members also need timed reservations. Arrange dining separately and do not depend on an unplanned late-night taxi.

local_ideas.title: NYBG Holiday Train Show after dark
